names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 22 iunie, «Sfântul Mucenic Zenon».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Ζήνων και Ζηνάς ο υπηρέτης του», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 22. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученик Зинон и Зина“ — Свети is not a rank and мученик is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the first of the two bare forenames is left. The «(22 June)» of the display name is the corpus’s own disambiguation and §10 reserves it. „официр римски“ is in the body and was never a candidate for the form. **The fold is deliberate, forced, and now the widest this wave has written**: `foldchk.py` returns six folders for «Зинон» — `zeno-20-april`, `zeno-companion-of-eudoxius`, `zeno-companion-of-peleus`, `zeno-of-diospolis`, `zeno-of-ikalto` and `zeno-of-nicomedia`, four of them `sr` and three `ru`, with `zeno-companion-of-peleus` holding the string in both languages — so this folder is the seventh, past the five of «Јулијан» yesterday. The heading offers nothing to break it with, and the folder has no by-name to offer either: its own display name disambiguates **by the day**, which is what a calendar that prints nothing but a name leaves you. A `READ_FOLDS` key is added for it in the same commit.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 22 июня ст. ст., «Зинон Филадельфийский (Аравийский), мч.», with the grade word left off; the folder already held the bare forename in Cyrillic off another calendar and this form is the fuller one, carrying both epithets.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the Greek line pairs him with Zenas exactly as doxologia's two bare lines for 22 iunie do. So this is the same pair, and saint.gr supplies what the Romanian source withheld: Philadelphia of Arabia, the eparch Maximus, and the year 303. The page's heading reads «(; - 303)» and its narrative «Το 303 μ.Χ. στη Φιλαδέλφεια της Αραβίας»; no `dates` object is proposed, because the year comes from the second source alone and is reported instead. He is none of the corpus's six other men of the name. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn under their line.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 05.07.2026 (22. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Зинон и Зина“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the master of its two men. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 22 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. The heading is quoted **whole** on both folders, as §4 requires. Note that its rank word is **singular** over two names, „Свети мученик Зинон и Зина“, where the 20 June company had мученици in the plural; §5 counts what the heading **enumerates**, which is two names, so it is two rows either way, and the singular is a fact about the book and not about the count. **`dates` STAYS NULL, AND A THIRD BOOK’S YEAR IS NOT WRITTEN FROM HERE.** This book gives no year: it dates the persecution „у време цара Максимијана“, in the time of the emperor Maximian, and an emperor is no source for a year and a reign is not a date. So nothing is written and `dates` is null before and after. **OPEN FOR THE AUTHOR, AND IT IS NOT THIS READER’S TO CLOSE**: saint.gr’s account, which is in this folder’s own prose, says the two lived at the beginning of the fourth century and that «In the year 303, at Philadelphia in Arabia, the eparch Maximus declared a persecution» — **a year this folder has cited and never recorded**, which is exactly what `date-citation-audit.mjs` exists to print. It is not written today because the Prologue is this day’s source and the Prologue gives no year; writing saint.gr’s 303 would be writing from a book this reading did not read. Maximian’s reign holds 303 comfortably, which is not a reason to write it. **A RANK WORD IN THE BODY, REFUSED TWICE OVER.** „Свети Зинон беше официр римски у граду Филаделфији Арабијској“ — a **Roman officer** in the city of Philadelphia in Arabia. The heading gives Свети, which is not a rank, and мученик, which is the `martyr` the folder carries, and nothing else; so `soldier` is refused on the standing rule that a rank inferred from the body is not written. **And it is refused a second time on its content**: saint.gr makes him not an officer at all but a rich Christian who shared out his possessions among the poor and freed all his slaves, of whom Zenas alone begged to stay. An officer and a rich layman who manumits his household are two different men’s lives, and a type written off a body that a second book contradicts would be the worst of both. Both are written in the life and neither is chosen. `types` UNTOUCHED, no `office` — no pack holds a phrase for a Roman officer, and offices go through the packs’ `offices` branch whose keys are English phrases the data already wrote down. THE DEATH DISAGREES TOO. saint.gr has the eparch Maximus have them both **beheaded** a few days after the arrests. This book: „најзад бачени у огањ, у који насуше незнабошци уља“ — at last thrown into a fire into which the pagans poured oil. Both written, neither chosen. The persecutor is војвода Максим here, a duke, where saint.gr has an eparch of the same name; he is no folder and takes no row. **New, and in no other book: the burial.** „телесни остаци бише сахрањени у цркви светог Георгија у месту званом Кипарисион“ — their bodies were buried in the church of Saint George in a place called Kyparision. **No row for any George**, of which the corpus keeps forty-nine: a dedication is not a relation, and an identification off a dedication’s name is not an identification. No `locations`: Philadelphia and Kyparision are named in clauses. ONE THING THE TWO BOOKS AGREE ON AND THE ROW ALREADY HOLDS. „А Зина му беше слуга“, Zenas was his servant, which is saint.gr’s «Ζηνάς ο υπηρέτης του» in Serbian; and that he was arrested because he came to visit his master in the prison, which saint.gr tells as a plea to the eparch for his master’s release. `zenas-the-martyr-22-june` is `related` here and the reciprocal is on that folder, both untouched. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 22 June is about the first entry and names its three men as three stars — „Јевсевије, и с њим Мелетије, Ко две звезде – трећа: Пелагије“ — and it opens „Црква никад није без пастира“, the Church is never without a shepherd. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **NOTHING IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER ON THIS DAY, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED BEFORE IN THIS WAVE.** The Prologue prints two entries for the Julian 22 June and the corpus holds every person in both headings: `eusebius-of-samosata` off two calendars, `zeno-the-martyr-22-june` and `zenas-the-martyr-22-june` off two more. Nineteen days before this one produced sixty-seven upgrades and no new folder, and four days in five refused somebody; this is the fifth day. It is worth recording as the shape of a day rather than as an absence: the corpus holds nine folders on the menologion 22/6 and this book names three of them and nobody else.
